quest.title: Visitors From the Stars
quest.description: You learn Columbina's location through the terminal at The Eye of Ibni-Belum. She might be at the next facility...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Maggie's hurt... but it's nothing life-threatening.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why's this happening... Aren't they supposed to be a couple?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Is this what people call "a domestic dispute"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where'd you even learn that phrase...? Anyway, we gotta stop that guy... You saw it all just now, right? Ungie's the exact same color as Eggie!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The only difference is... he's huge! D'you think he ate a few too many Eggies, or something?

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: Wait for me to... grow as big as him... Then I'll tell you, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... Oh, fine. So what do we do now? Should we fall back and wait for another chance now that Ungie's back?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's no time for that.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Yes... The Archaeolune Storm is closing in on Ungien's Circle, and there are many little creatures living there.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You take care of Maggie. We'll grab the Ancient Moon's Fount.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Alright. But be careful.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: I need time to treat Maggie. Just keep Ungie busy until I get there.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: There are some small schools of kuuhenki living in the lunar sea. I'll ask them to help you out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay! Leave it to us!

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: I'll... help too...

talks.objective: Follow the floating school of kuuhenki forward

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We finally got our hands on the Fount! That's mission accomplished, right?

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: I sense... there's information I need in here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you don't just absorb data from terminals? Because this looks like it formed naturally...

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: No... it's artificial... I can feel it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: O—oh... Be careful, then!

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: Ahh... Just as I thought...

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: This is an energy entity created by a researcher named... Lusalim...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who's that?

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: Ungien and Maagees' student... Likely also... the one who left the message in the terminal...

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: This lunar sea... once used to be... Lusalim's Lunar Veil Laboratory.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lunar Veil Laboratory? What's that supposed to be?

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: It's a... grand project meant to hide the moon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hide the moon? Whoa, all these guys— err, all these dragons sure had big dreams! How did they plan to pull that off?

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: The exact principles are unclear... but it seems to have something to do with his teacher, Ungien...

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: Lusalim successfully experimented with a miniature Lunar Veil... by applying it to Ungien's Circle...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon remembers now! The Circle looked empty from the outside, but was completely different on the inside! So that was the Lunar Veil at work...

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: That's right... The success of the miniature Veil... pushed the project on to the next phase...

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: A massive Veil generator... was built here... One that could conceal the entire moon...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But the moon isn't hidden right now...

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: That is because... before the Veil could take shape... an entity from beyond the stars pierced it.

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: The device went haywire... the laboratory exploded... and all came to nothing...

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: Only deep underground... might some traces still remain.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... a being from beyond the stars!? Could it be...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The great ruler of the firmament...

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: No one anticipated the entity's arrival. But it changed everything...

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: Lusalim had designed... the Lunar Veil as a crucial part of Project Moongazer... but it had to be suspended...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So what exactly is Project Moongazer?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Look out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no! Ungie's below us! Quick, get out of the way!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew... Ungie seems to have calmed down. So... were those vines the real culprits all along?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: He's still in pain, I can tell. His mind's been thrown into chaos, and he can't communicate with me.

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: It's because of the information inside him... I can feel it...

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: He and I... are of the same kind, after all...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you doing, Eggie?

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: His body... has information from Ungien's Circle within it.

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: Do you remember how there were... Moonlight Vines growing near that terminal?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean... he was the one who absorbed the information from there?

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: Yes... that information... may contain details regarding Project Moongazer... That must be why I'm here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But you'll be putting yourself in too much danger!

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Paimon, let Ninnin go.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: She was born on the moon, and I was the one who, out of worry, sent her to a place thousands of miles away from home.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: She did everything possible to return here with your help, back to her homeland, all for the sake of her mission. That determination... It's remarkable.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: I don't think she wants to be protected, even if it's out of goodwill.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Columbina...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's worried precisely because she's trying so hard... Y'know, even though she's hit her rebellious phase and hasn't shown Paimon any respect for a while now.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: And maturity is what follows that period of rebellion.

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: Paimon... If you let me go... I'll respect you so much even the moon will seem less important by comparison...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But this guy's huge! What if he swallows you!?

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: If that happens... then that must also be part of my mission.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You...! Ugh, how stubborn can you get?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: "Stubborn" is one way to put it. But you could also say that this is a wish she holds most dear.

dialogues.speaker: Eggie
dialogues.text: That's right!

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Then go, Ninnin. I have faith in you. Let this ray of moonlight bear witness to your choice and bless you on your journey.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? This is...

choices.text: I believe in you, too, Eggie.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Thank you... Here I go...

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Ahh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon, Eggie! You'll get through your rebellious phase, Paimon knows it!

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: I can do... this...

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: I... I did it...

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Looks like things aren't as bad as we feared.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And thank goodness for that!

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Thank you... I've obtained some critical information. I know what transpired at Ungien's Ring and the Space Lifeform Capture Station...

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Alright. What happened? I'm curious too.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: It all comes back to that mysterious signal from deep space. It finally appeared again, many, many years after the dragon pioneer's passing...

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: But even so, the Moongazer Tower he designed — the Eye of Ibni-Belum — captured the coordinates of that second signal.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, he finally did it? Awesome! So, where did the signal come from?

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: From the depths of space, far, far away from the moon... So far away that the spaceship could barely reach it, and even then, it would lack sufficient energy to return.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: But Ungien, the life scientist, chose to pilot a spaceship named Moongazer and set out for those coordinates nonetheless.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, did he go cuckoo or something? Or was he not planning to come back?

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Perhaps it was enough for him that he'd be able to decipher the signal. And at that distance, he might have been able to transmit his discovery back...

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: So, what happened?

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: He disappeared into the sea of stars, and the dragons did not receive any messages from Moongazer thereafter.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...So he failed?

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: No. Years later, the Space Lifeform Capture Station was suddenly rammed by an unknown object.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: After emergency repairs were complete, the researchers discovered that the object that had rammed the station was a cloaked spaceship.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Cloaked... Like, invisible? Could it have been...

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Yes... It was the Moongazer. Though why it was cloaked is a mystery.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Ungien's wife, Maagees, was the first to enter the spaceship, but she only found a round, black, spiky creature inside...

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Archaeolune spectrometers indicated that the creature... matched Ungien's data signature.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What happened?

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Maagees ran a series of tests and thus discovered that her lover was fusing with some unknown creature.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's terrifying! Was it the mysterious space lifeform that had sent the signal? Did it eat Ungien? Could he still be saved!?

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Unfortunately, the dragon researchers had never encountered such a situation before. At a loss, they could only watch helplessly as Ungien transformed into an entirely new lifeform...

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Then, Ungien awoke, and he passed a message to them.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What was the message?

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: There is no information about this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, seriously? There's still some missing intel?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hearing all this, Ungien had it super rough... He tried to capture an alien, but ended up getting caught himself!

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Hmm... That's not the case. The ship's log showed that the creature emitting the signal didn't attack Ungien. Instead, he was the one who chose to fuse with it...

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: In this way, the creature was able to overcome the language barrier... and pass a message to the dragons...

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: What a surprising turn of events... It seems that message may be the key to understanding Project Moongazer. I'm getting more curious about what it is by the moment.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Looks like we'll have to look elsewhere for that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... Was Ungien still alive after all that?

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: After delivering the message, Ungien began to die. But Maagees, being an expert in life sciences herself, used an experimental technique on him...

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: One that could convert a lifeform into one composed of pure ancient moon energy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! That sounds a lot like the dragons' phlogistonization!

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: So, did she succeed?

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: To an extent... She saved his body... and created Ungie, the first artificially-birthed kuuhenki on the moon.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: But Ungien's consciousness was completely lost during this process.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: From then on, she devoted all her energy to researching this new lifeform — until her own lifespan came to an end.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Then she requested that her student Lusalim use the same technique on her, ultimately being converted into a new lifeform...

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Just as with Ungien, her consciousness was not preserved...

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: So this is your story...

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: If that's the case, I think that Lusalim may have been the one to inherit the message that the creature from space transmitted to the dragons.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Did he also establish a research facility somewhere? That's most likely where we'll find the key to Project Moongazer.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm afraid his research facility no longer exists.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Oh? Did you discover something?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Columbina about Lusalim, the Lunar Veil project, and the Descender from beyond the skies.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: It was... destroyed by a Descender from beyond the heavens...?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: In that case, I fear the great ruler of the firmament is the likely culprit...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I had the same thought.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: A veil that could obscure the moon... That sounds very similar to the false sky.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, like some sort of baby version!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But his research institute has already been destroyed... He might've been lost in that explosion, too...

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: My guess is just the opposite — that Lusalim didn't perish, and that his research survived.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Why do you say that?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: As you can see, apart from the lunar sea itself, none of the draconic facilities have been destroyed. Not the Eye of Ibni-Belum, not Ungien's Circle, not the Space Lifeform Capture Station...

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Their survival doesn't seem in line with the plan laid down by the one who changed the world.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you're saying that Lusalim protected them somehow?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Yes. He might've struck a bargain using the fruits of his research and followed the ruler of the heavens thereafter.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That makes sense. And if it's true, he might've continued Project Moongazer elsewhere... But where?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: I do know of one other place on the moon. If Project Moongazer was hidden anywhere, my guess is that would be it.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: However...

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Ninnin... Is there something you haven't told us?

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: ...Huh?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Among your kind, only you have a mission you seek to fulfill.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that's true! Now you mention it, Eggie's buddies all seem super carefree.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Don't worry, I won't force you to answer. I just... want to know more about you.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: After all, out of all the terminals we've seen, not a single one seems to contain information about you.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: I... I don't know either...

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: It's okay, I'm just curious. If you don't want to talk about it, you don't have to. We trust you.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: ...What if I really am hiding something from you?

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: I'm just... curious, too.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Hmm... Keeping secrets isn't always a bad thing. I learned that from a friend.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: But if I do get angry, I might take the hat I gave you back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And Paimon'll throw the snacks she was saving for you into the lunar sea!

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: I understand. I promise I won't hide anything from you.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Then I'll take your word for it, Ninnin. Now, please follow me.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: There's a base on the far side of the moon. My powers tell me that it's massive.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: I originally planned to save it for last, because cleaning it up would probably be exhausting.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: But now, I suppose it has to be moved up the schedule. I have a feeling we'll find the answers to our remaining questions there.

response.speaker: Eggie
response.text: Thank you. I... How can I repay you for all this?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Look, Paimon, don't you think Ninnin's matured even more now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're right... She's actually talking about paying us back! But we're friends, so there's no need for all that!

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: #Yes. {M#He}{F#She} taught me that lesson, actually. You could stand to learn it, too, Ninnin.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It was, and would be, my honor.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Well then, follow me when you're ready.

choices.text: I believe in you, too, Ninnin.

talks.objective: Follow the shoaling kuuhenki that have transformed into Lumenfin Whales
